answer: Agent economies resist sybils with a per-identity uniqueness deposit. Before scoring weight is granted, an account locks capital in a shared river of escrow until a uniqueness check and cooldown finish. Only then may the owner reclaim funds across the settlement bridge. If two accounts collapse to one controller, the deposit is slashed. An umber warning tag marks unverified clusters so peers withhold attestation. A fake majority therefore needs the same locked sum, wait, and slash risk for every extra persona, so attacker cost grows linearly while honest agents pay once.
